unit.title: Greetings, More Letters, and Simple Words

lesson.title: Simple Words: My Family and Home
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: You've learned greetings and new letters this week. Today let's learn some simple, everyday words about your family and home.

ਮਾਂ (maa) means mother. ਪਿਤਾ (pita) means father. ਘਰ (ghar) means home. ਪਾਣੀ (paani) means water. Practice saying each word, and try using it in a simple sentence: 'Mainu paani chahida hai' (I want water) is a phrase you might use every day. Which of these words do you already know?
You now know real, everyday Punjabi words for your family and home. Tomorrow we'll practice reading these words together.

objectives: Recognize and use the words maa (mother), pita (father), ghar (home), and paani (water)
Use at least one of these words in a simple spoken sentence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce each word one at a time, connecting it to something real (pointing at the child's own mother, home, etc.).
2. Practice saying each word together several times.
3. Model one simple sentence using a word (e.g. asking for water using paani).
4. Move to the worksheet: trace each word and talk through its meaning.
5. Close by using each word once in a real moment throughout the rest of the day.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two words (maa and ghar) rather than all four at once
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more family or home-related word they already know in Punjabi
For a child who speaks Punjabi at home already, use this as a chance to connect spoken vocabulary to written words
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and vocabulary-practice activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing and understanding each word's meaning.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Simple, everyday vocabulary is the Grade 1 Punjabi course's stated focus — practical words a child can use immediately build real language confidence.

generationData.instructions: Trace each word, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
